top_choice_rationale: P001 rests on one identifiable invention, Katori's magic-wavelength lattice, which cancels the clock-transition light shift while many atoms are held in the Lamb-Dicke regime. It was carried to the 10^-18 level, reproduced and exceeded by independent laboratories, and the shift physics (polarisabilities, blackbody radiation, higher-order light shifts) is well controlled. The two-name allocation (Katori for the concept, Ye for taking strontium to the accuracy and stability frontier and into many-body regimes) is the cleanest on the slate, and a narrow citation keeps it distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. P002 is a mature, reproduced new class of matter, but Bernevig, Hughes and the late Zhang, and the 3D work, fall outside the three names, so its allocation is structurally incomplete. Either award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: Long-running collaboration with Anne L'Huillier and papers with the Lund attosecond group and Ursula Keller's ETH group (field adjacent to precision AMO, though no documented link to Katori or Ye); no apparent connection to Kane, Mele or Molenkamp from the profile.
